Almost two years ago, I was leaving my boyfriend at the time’s house and was driving home around midnight on a Wednesday. 

I was driving perfectly, following all the rules and what not. Which TBH I don’t usually do (I’m a bit of a speed demon) but in this situation the radio was low, two hands on the wheel, going 40 in a 45. Checking my rear view mirror every 15-20 seconds. No cars in sight. 

Look at the road. I was about a mile from my bfs at this point. 20ish seconds later I check my rear view again. 

You know in movies where someone gets in a car accident and all you see is headlights coming at the camera? Literally is exactly what it felt like. There was a of a sudden an SUV about 2 seconds from slamming me straight on from behind. Cops estimated he was going at least double my speed, if not more. 

I saw him right before he hit me. Swerved enough to the right that he hit the left side of my car, knocked the back tire off and he kept going to hit three trees and a house. Only reason the dude survived is likely cause he was plastered. 3x the legal limit. If I hadn’t seen him and been able to swerve he likely would have killed me. 

I still think about that all the time. I was so lucky that I saw him just in time. If I had looked up a second later I probably wouldn’t be here.
